questions.question: What fertilizer is best for paddy?

answer.summary: The best fertilizer depends on the soil test, but a balanced NPK application along with organic manure is generally recommended.

recommended_fertilizers.name: DAP (Diammonium Phosphate)
recommended_fertilizers.purpose: Provides phosphorus and nitrogen during early growth

recommended_fertilizers.name: MOP (Muriate of Potash)
recommended_fertilizers.purpose: Improves grain filling and disease resistance

recommended_fertilizers.name: Vermicompost
recommended_fertilizers.purpose: Enhances microbial activity and nutrient availability

answer.recommended_npk: 120:60:40 kg/ha (may vary by state and soil test)
application_schedule: Apply full phosphorus and potassium as basal dose.
Split nitrogen into 2-3 applications during crop growth.
tips: Conduct a soil test before fertilizer application.
Avoid excessive nitrogen as it increases pest and disease incidence.
Maintain proper irrigation after fertilizer application.

questions.question: How can I control pests naturally?

answer.summary: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and biological control methods are recommended before using chemical pesticides.
natural_methods: Neem oil spray (3-5 ml/L of water)
Install yellow sticky traps for sucking pests
Remove and destroy infected plant parts
Encourage beneficial insects like ladybird beetles and lacewings
tips: Spray chemicals only when pest population exceeds threshold.

questions.question: My tomato leaves are turning yellow.

answer.summary: Yellowing of tomato leaves may result from nutrient deficiency, overwatering, diseases, pests, or environmental stress.

possible_causes.symptoms: Yellow leaves with poor root growth.
Yellow leaves with dark concentric spots.
Yellowing starts on one side of the plant.
Yellow leaves with curling and sticky honeydew.

recommended_actions: Apply balanced fertilizer if nutrient deficiency is suspected.
Consult local agricultural experts if symptoms persist.
prevention: Apply fertilizers based on soil test.
